steps.what: Interpret the commercial brief, timing constraints and permitted musical material
Compose and audition the melody, harmony, instrumentation and picture cues
outputs: original musical composition and cue choices

steps.what: Prepare the actual score using the chosen instrumentation and cue structure
inputs: original musical composition and cue choices

steps.what: Listen against picture and correct the finished music and score

tasks.design: Use a native {OTHER} notation template for recurring staff labels and cue headings while the composer writes and auditions the music. OTHER denotes notation and audio-production software; the author saves the score during writing without a separate approval stage.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated score furniture had to be entered alongside original composition.
tasks.enabler_now: A reusable staff and cue layout removes a small amount of engraving, not composition.
tasks.still_hard: Originality, emotional fit, musical quality and exact synchronisation remain the composer's work.
tasks.human_edge: The composer decides what the advertisement or scene should sound like.
tasks.altitude: A small notation improvement inside composition.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: notation templates can retain staff labels and layout while composition remains manual.

assumptions: Illustrative shares are hypotheses, not measured baselines.
The current score preparation includes recurring labels and headings not already templated; if already present, the saving is zero.
The task ends with checked music; client delivery is not silently included.
unknowns: Frequency of repeat ensembles and cue structures
research_questions: How much score preparation is recurring furniture rather than musical entry?

already_counted.description: Check the populated score, timing and any template corrections in s3 and s4.

incremental.description: Amortised maintenance of the recurring score layout.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Reused headings remove 10*0.10=1 hour less 0.3 upkeep, net 0.7. Cautious case: a unique cue structure permits only 0.4 hours of staff-label reuse, leaving 0.1 net; the rest is composed and engraved manually.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check source notation and the musician's range, clef and transposing instrument
outputs: verified source and target interval, range and clef

steps.what: Transpose the selected notes and key signatures into the target part
inputs: verified source and target interval, range and clef

steps.what: Check sounding pitches and repair spelling, range, clef and unplayable passages
Adjust page turns and legibility in the actual transposed score

tasks.design: Apply the {OTHER} notation application's native interval transposition to a verified selection, then inspect the sounding result and repair instrument-specific problems. OTHER means music notation software; paper-source entry and conversion checks belong in s1 rather than arriving free.
tasks.previous_blocker: Individual pitch and key edits can duplicate exact interval arithmetic.
tasks.enabler_now: Native transposition applies the interval to a selected part in one operation.
tasks.still_hard: Enharmonic spelling, playable range, instrument conventions and phrase suitability need inspection.
tasks.human_edge: The musician's actual abilities determine whether a technically correct part works.
tasks.altitude: Replace repeated pitch edits with one bounded notation operation.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native music notation software supports selected-part interval transposition.

assumptions: Shares are unmeasured hypotheses for work that still edits pitches individually.
If native transposition already performs s2, its incremental saving is zero.
The low case has a partly illegible paper source: only 6 baseline hours of pitch editing can use the operation; the rest is retained for source reconstruction and correction.
research_questions: Which portions can be selected confidently without rebuilding the source?

already_counted.description: Source capture, interval selection and conversion verification are retained in s1; sounding-pitch and range repairs stay in s3.

incremental.description: Amortised rehearsal of instrument presets and exceptional notation tests.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Native transposition removes 35 pitch-editing hours less 1 upkeep, net 34. Cautious case: a partly illegible paper score requires manual reconstruction and only 6 hours can use transposition, leaving 5 net; source entry and all musical checks remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Rewrite scores in another musical style

steps.what: Study the original score and choose the new style and expressive intentions
Rewrite rhythms, harmonies and phrasing in the actual musical score
Enter recurring tempo indications and playback markings for the chosen interpretation
outputs: score with tempo and playback markings

steps.what: Audition and revise the rewritten score for musical coherence and intended style
inputs: score with tempo and playback markings

tasks.design: Keep the stylistic rewrite with the composer and configure native {OTHER} reusable tempo and playback markings for repeated indications. OTHER is notation and playback software; the actual rewritten score is authored and saved in s2 through s4 without an author approval gate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated playback and tempo indications can require repetitive entry during a rewrite.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable notation markings remove repeated parameter entry after the composer chooses their meaning.
tasks.still_hard: A new style demands musical judgement beyond changing a tempo value.
tasks.human_edge: The composer hears whether altered harmony and rhythm form a convincing interpretation.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated notation entry within a human stylistic rewrite.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: notation applications can reuse tempo and playback indications.

assumptions: Shares and cuts are provisional, not measurements.
Only repeated indication parameter entry is removed; selecting placement and listening stay.
For a through-composed score with mostly unique rubato, only 0.6 baseline hours of repeated markings can be reused; the rest of s3 remains.
unknowns: Number of repeated versus unique indications
research_questions: Do recurring markings occupy enough entry time to justify maintaining a preset?

already_counted.description: Place and check markings in s3 and audition their musical effects in s4.

incremental.description: Amortised maintenance and playback testing of indication presets.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Reused markings remove 10*0.20=2 hours less 0.4 upkeep, net 1.6. Cautious case: unique rubato permits only 0.6 hours of repeated indication entry to be removed, leaving 0.2 net; bespoke markings stay manual.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange another composer's music for desired effects

steps.what: Study the source music, permitted use, target ensemble and intended musical effects
Set up the target score staves, instrument names and part layout
Write the changed voicings, textures and musical material into the arrangement
Listen, check instrumental feasibility and revise the actual arrangement and parts
outputs: checked arrangement achieving the intended effects

tasks.design: Reuse a native {OTHER} ensemble score template to populate recurring staff identities and part layout, then write and audition the arrangement manually. OTHER denotes notation and playback software; checking source permissions remains part of studying the actual commission.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recurring ensemble score structures can be rebuilt for each arrangement.
tasks.enabler_now: An ensemble template can supply staff identity and layout without choosing musical content.
tasks.still_hard: Voicing, balance, instrumental technique and the desired expressive effect remain manual.
tasks.human_edge: The arranger decides how another composer's material should sound in this ensemble.
tasks.altitude: Reuse score structure while keeping arrangement decisions with the musician.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: ensemble templates can populate notation staves and part layouts.

assumptions: The proposed shares are unmeasured hypotheses.
Three baseline hours removed from s2 represent recurring staff and part setup, while nine remain for adaptation.
For an unusual mixed ensemble only 0.8 hours of staff naming can be reused; instrument mappings and layout are rebuilt manually.
No separate submission or performance release is part of this arrangement-only estimate.
research_questions: Which target ensembles recur without substantial layout reconstruction?

already_counted.description: Adapt the target structure in s2 and check playability and part layout in s4.

incremental.description: Amortised maintenance of the ensemble template.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Recurring ensemble setup removes 12*0.25=3 hours less 0.5 upkeep, net 2.5. Cautious case: an unusual mixed ensemble permits only 0.8 hours of staff-name reuse, leaving 0.3 net while mappings and layout are rebuilt manually.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use precise notation operations for mechanical score work while retaining musical authorship.
skills_to_grow: Check sounding and written pitch separately
Measure notation work separately from composition
role.ambitious_version: A composer uses verified notation operations and spends the recovered time on musical decisions and listening.
